scope: Host/origin validation, DNS/IPv6 handling, forwarding headers, rebinding protection and transport options (src/http.ts, src/config.ts, src/serve.ts, src/serve-command.ts, src/runtime.ts, src/cli.ts, src/cli/client.ts, src/metrics.ts, src/settings/{load,inspect}.ts)

findings.title: SWARMFORGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS entries are matched case-sensitively, so valid hostname spellings (uppercase, trailing root dot, embedded port) are silently dead and every request returns a bare 403
findings.evidence: src/http.ts:9-19 builds the allowlist Set from the raw config strings (SWARMFORGE_HOST at line 13, split/trim of SWARMFORGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS at lines 14-16) and compares with `hosts.has(url.hostname)` at line 18. WHATWG URL lowercases the authority, so `new URL(request.url).hostname` is always lower-case and never contains a port. src/config.ts:10-12 (`loopbackHosts`/`isLoopbackHost`) lowercases for its own comparison, proving case-insensitivity is the intended semantics. src/config.ts:16-24 (`acceptedHosts`) only checks that a token exists; it never checks that an entry is matchable.
findings.reproduction: Real Bun.serve listener, valid bearer on every request, only the allowed_hosts spelling varies (/tmp/opencode/review20/probe/allowlist-probe.ts, log /workspace/.swarmforge/logs/host-allowlist-probe.log): allowed_hosts="MCP.Example.Test" with Host: MCP.Example.Test -> HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden; allowed_hosts="Mcp.Example.Test" -> 403; allowed_hosts="mcp.example.test" -> 200 OK; allowed_hosts="mcp.example.test:8787" -> 403. Control isolating the cause: Host: LOCALHOST reaches 200 OK against the default config whose allowlist holds only lowercase `localhost` (/workspace/.swarmforge/logs/host-wire-probe.log), proving normalisation happens on the wire side only.
findings.consequence: A reverse-proxy deployment configured exactly as docs/ENVIRONMENT.md:33 instructs accepts the value, enforces the token, then refuses /health, /events and /mcp with 403 and no log or startup diagnostic, so the operator diagnoses a credential or networking fault instead of the accepted-host list.
findings.recommendation: Lower-case and strip a trailing root dot from each config entry when building the set in src/http.ts (normalise IPv6 entries to bracketed form), and add a superRefine issue on SWARMFORGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS in src/config.ts rejecting any entry containing ':', differing from its own lower-case form, or ending in '.', so `swarmforge config validate` and startup fail loudly. Newly exposed as `server.allowed_hosts` at src/settings/load.ts:272-277.

findings.title: Origin is compared against url.origin, so any TLS-terminating reverse proxy - the documented deployment shape - rejects every request that carries an Origin header
findings.evidence: src/http.ts:30-32: `const origin = request.headers.get("origin"); if (origin && origin !== url.origin) return 403`. `url.origin` is derived from the plaintext listener connection plus the forwarded Host, so it is always the http backend origin. No Forwarded / X-Forwarded-Proto handling exists anywhere in the repo. The SDK's own `enableDnsRebindingProtection` is left at its default false (node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/server/webStandardStreamableHttp.js:79), so nothing downstream compensates.
findings.reproduction: Real listener, allowed host and valid bearer on every request, only Host/Origin pairing varies (/tmp/opencode/review20/probe/allowlist-probe.ts, log /workspace/.swarmforge/logs/host-allowlist-probe.log): Host: mcp.example.test + Origin: https://mcp.example.test -> 403; Host: mcp.example.test:443 + Origin: https://mcp.example.test -> 403; control Host: mcp.example.test + Origin: http://mcp.example.test -> 406 Not Acceptable, i.e. it passed the origin check and reached the MCP transport, proving the 403 is the origin comparison.
findings.consequence: For the TLS-terminating proxy that docs/ENVIRONMENT.md:33 ('for a reverse proxy') and the README ('Deploy TLS ... externally') direct operators to use, every origin-aware client gets 403 on all routes including /health and /events, since the check precedes routing. No diagnostic distinguishes a TLS terminator from a hostile origin.
findings.recommendation: Derive accepted origins from configuration instead of the plaintext connection: either treat Origin as advisory once the host allowlist has pinned the authority and a bearer token is configured, or add an explicit SWARMFORGE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS list and/or opt-in X-Forwarded-Proto/Forwarded scheme trust restricted to already-bearer-authenticated requests (trimming default :443/:80). If neither, document at docs/ENVIRONMENT.md:33 that a terminating proxy must rewrite Origin, and add the missing positive test.

findings.title: The metrics listener enforces neither the host allowlist nor the bearer token on the same bind host the config validator protects
findings.evidence: src/serve.ts:177-191 binds metrics to config.SWARMFORGE_HOST and serves /metrics from an inline fetch with no host validation and no credential check, unlike the API handler at src/http.ts:9-29. src/config.ts:135-141 raises the non-loopback token requirement based on acceptedHosts, which covers only the MCP surface.
findings.reproduction: Real startServer with SWARMFORGE_HOST=0.0.0.0 and SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN set (/tmp/opencode/review20/probe/metrics-probe.ts, log /workspace/.swarmforge/logs/host-metrics-probe.log): API listener 18787 -> Host: 127.0.0.1 = 401, Host: evil.example = 403; metrics listener 19090 -> Host: 127.0.0.1 = 200, Host: evil.example = 200, Host: attacker-controlled.example = 200, all with no credential, exposing team labels and worker/inference/token counters from src/metrics.ts.
findings.consequence: A deployment satisfying every documented configuration check can still leave Prometheus telemetry world-readable on a wildcard bind; the 401/403 on the API surface creates a false impression that the deployment is authenticated.
findings.recommendation: Route the metrics fetch through the same host allowlist (403 on a non-allowlisted Host) and/or require an explicit opt-in before binding metrics to a non-loopback SWARMFORGE_HOST; add a 403 test for an arbitrary Host on the metrics port. Documented at docs/ENVIRONMENT.md:45 ('Protect externally if public'), hence LOW rather than higher.

findings.title: Startup banner prints an invalid URL for IPv6 binds, including the wildcard ::
findings.evidence: src/runtime.ts:50-56 interpolates the raw host: line 50 special-cases 0.0.0.0 only, line 53 emits `http://${host}:${info.port}/mcp`. Reached from src/serve-command.ts:148-161, which passes config.SWARMFORGE_HOST unchanged while taking the port from the correctly bracketed handle.url. Contrast src/serve.ts:110-113, whose origin() brackets IPv6.
findings.reproduction: /tmp/opencode/review20/probe/ipv6-probe.ts against the real modules (log /workspace/.swarmforge/logs/host-ipv6-probe.log): real renderStartup gives host=::1 -> 'MCP       http://::1:8787/mcp' and host=:: -> 'MCP       http://:::8787/mcp'; a real startServer bound to ::1 reports handle.url = http://[::1]:8787 while the banner says http://::1:8787/mcp, and fetch to http://[::1]:port/health returns 200 {"status":"ok"} - so the server is correct and only the rendered URL is unparseable.
findings.consequence: On a TTY the operator cannot copy the advertised endpoint for an IPv6 or IPv6-wildcard deployment; the `bun run status` hint cannot be acted on.
findings.recommendation: Share one IPv6-bracketing helper between renderStartup and serve.ts:origin(), and map :: to [::1] in the same way line 50 maps 0.0.0.0 to 127.0.0.1. Pre-existing at the target, not introduced by this branch; tests/serve.test.ts binds only 127.0.0.1 so IPv6 rendering is never exercised.

verified_good: Exact url.hostname allowlist evaluated on the wire authority before routing and before /health, /events and /mcp; Host: evil.example -> 403 in every configuration probed.
Duplicate Host headers: the first wins and is what is validated (Host: evil.example first, Host: localhost second -> 403).
Absolute-form request-target authority is what is validated (RFC 9112 3.2.2): GET http://localhost/health with Host: evil.example -> 403.
X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-For are ignored entirely - no spoofable forwarding-header trust.
Ordering is host (403) then bearer (401) then origin (403), so an unlisted host is not probed for credentials.
Wire Host is case-insensitive (URL lowercases), so Host: LOCALHOST matches the lowercase allowlist entry.
